status_key.primary: Opened the primary record (DOI page, regulator page, SEC filing, or the paper itself).
status_key.secondary: Seen only in a search excerpt or a news / law-firm summary of the primary document. Re-check before quoting.
status_key.vendor: Claim made by the company selling the product. No independent audit found.

studies.study: Berg, Burg, Gombovic & Puri (2020), Review of Financial Studies
studies.finding: Digital footprint (AUC 0.696) beats a credit-bureau score (0.683); combined 0.736. Works for people without a bureau score.
studies.ours: Supports our central idea. Our alternative-data gain on simulated data (+4.8 points) is the same size as theirs (+5.3).
studies.caveat: Our gain is built into the simulation; theirs is measured on real purchases.

studies.study: Bjorkegren & Grissen (2020), World Bank Economic Review
studies.data: Phone records matched to loans at a South American telecom
studies.finding: Riskiest fifth of borrowers default 2.8 times as often as the safest fifth; beats bureau models on thin files.
studies.ours: Our model's riskiest-to-safest fifth ratio is shown in the benchmark table below.
studies.caveat: Different country, product and signal. Compare the metric, not the data.

studies.study: Agarwal, Alok, Ghosh & Gupta (2020), working paper
studies.finding: Credit score alone AUC 0.59, phone and social footprint alone 0.604. About 129 million Indians were mostly denied credit for lack of history.
studies.ours: The honest warning: real Indian data is much harder than our simulation. Expect a lower AUC on real borrowers.

studies.study: Alok, Ghosh, Kulkarni & Puri (2024), NBER WP 33259
studies.data: India's UPI rollout and the universe of consumer loans
studies.finding: UPI expanded formal credit to new-to-credit borrowers; fintechs were the only lenders reaching people with no credit history, with no evidence of higher default.
studies.ours: Justifies UPI-style features and the gig / thin-file segment in India.
studies.caveat: Policy study, not a scoring benchmark.

studies.finding: Several methods beat logistic regression; heterogeneous ensembles rank best; random forest recommended as a minimum benchmark.
studies.ours: Our model menu (logistic, forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) follows this. We re-ran it on four real datasets: gradient boosting is best or tied on all four.
studies.caveat: Per-dataset AUC values were not verified.

studies.study: Gunnarsson, vanden Broucke, Baesens, Oskarsdottir & Lemahieu (2021), EJOR
studies.finding: XGBoost best; deep neural networks no better and costlier.
studies.ours: Matches our choice of boosted trees.

studies.study: Makridakis, Spiliotis & Assimakopoulos (2018), PLOS ONE and IJF (M3 / M4)
studies.finding: Pure ML forecasters were beaten by statistical methods; simple benchmarks are hard to beat.
studies.ours: Supports SARIMAX for the portfolio forecast. On real Indian NPL data SARIMAX had error 0.48 pp against 2.04 pp for the naive forecast.

studies.study: Gibbs & Candes (2021), NeurIPS: Adaptive Conformal Inference
studies.finding: Adaptive intervals keep long-run coverage close to target under distribution shift.
studies.ours: On real US delinquency data our adaptive range covers 80.9% against 72.3% for the plain model range (target 80%).
studies.caveat: Theory bound is loose at 94 quarters; we report empirical coverage.

products.name: TransUnion CIBIL score
products.uses: Repayment history from member lenders; score 300-900
products.evidence: No public accuracy study found. Bureau scores need an existing credit history (a lender blog says about 6 months; not confirmed by TransUnion).
products.gap_we_fill: People with no history get no score. Fintech small-ticket loans are mostly NTC.

products.name: CRIF High Mark with CreditVidya
products.uses: Phone and app data, transaction data. A 2017 report says it used calls, contacts and browsing history.
products.evidence: Partnership announced 2019 to score thin-file customers. A marketplace listing claims it is twice as effective as bureau scores; no study found.
products.gap_we_fill: Open method with explanations. RBI's 2025 digital-lending rules restrict reading call logs and contacts, so older data sources may need review.

products.name: FICO Score XD
products.uses: Telecom, cable and utility payments, public records and property data
products.evidence: FICO says it scores more than 70% of previously unscorable applicants. This is coverage, not accuracy; no Gini figure found.
products.gap_we_fill: Our model outputs a calibrated default probability, reasons and stress tests, not only a score.

products.name: Upstart
products.uses: Machine-learning model on bureau plus alternative data
products.evidence: CFPB review of its 2017 no-action letter found 27% more approvals and 16% lower average APR than a traditional model, with no fair-lending disparities flagged. Upstart's own 10-K reports 43.4% more approvals and 43.2% lower APR (internal study, December 2021).
products.gap_we_fill: Our equal-loss test on simulated data gives a comparable metric (more approvals at the same default rate), but ours is not on real loans.

products.name: Zest AI
products.evidence: Case studies say 22% more approvals at no added risk (one credit union), 30-40% lower delinquency (another) and a 25% approval lift with 20% less risk in a preliminary test. No independent audit found.
products.gap_we_fill: Open code and a re-runnable validation suite.

products.name: Tala and Branch
products.evidence: Tala reports repayment above 90%. No published AUC or independent validation of its model found. The nearest academic evidence is Bjorkegren & Grissen (2.8x risk ratio).
products.gap_we_fill: Published validation results and per-decision explanations.

products.name: EFL psychometric scoring
products.evidence: Independent Peru evaluation (IDB, Arraiz, Bruhn & Stucchi) found it can lower portfolio risk as a second screen. AUC 0.57-0.66 in a Harvard-affiliated abstract. Another study found weak results for similar tests.
products.gap_we_fill: Uses behavioural data rather than answers that applicants can game.

products.name: Account Aggregator rails (India)
products.uses: Consent-based bank and financial data transfer
products.evidence: Sahamati reports about Rs 3.82 lakh crore of loans across 3.68 crore loans in FY26 (8.4% of retail and MSME lending by value). A CRIF-Sahamati report finds a 28.5% new-to-credit share in mid-ticket AA loans.
products.gap_we_fill: AA supplies data; it does not decide. IntelliCredit is a decision layer that could sit on top.

products.name: Bank-style logistic scorecard
products.uses: Application form fields and past loans
products.evidence: We built it and measured it on the same data. See the head-to-head section.
products.gap_we_fill: Measured directly, so this is the only like-for-like competitor in the dashboard.

regulation.says: Covers automated credit assessment. The borrower must get a Key Fact Statement before the loan is finalised; money moves directly between borrower and lender. Our literature pack also notes that lending apps may not read call logs or contacts.
regulation.ours: Uses consent-style signals (UPI, utility, recharge, balances). Each decision comes with reasons that can feed the Key Fact Statement.

regulation.says: Seven principles including Fairness and Explainability, and 26 recommendations. Summaries say credit and underwriting models should be explainable, auditable and free of bias.
regulation.ours: Per-applicant SHAP reasons, a stored subgroup-performance table, and an open, re-runnable method.

regulation.says: Lenders using complex algorithms must still give the specific principal reasons for a refusal.
regulation.ours: Top SHAP drivers per applicant; counterfactual recourse goes further.

regulation.rule: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and CICRA 2005 (India)
regulation.says: Personal data needs consent and a stated purpose; credit information is restricted to regulated members.
regulation.ours: This is why borrower data here is simulated: no real person's data is used. A live deployment would need consent flows.
